Objective To investigate relationships between serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (sUCHL1), tau (sTau) and glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP) levels and disease activity/disability in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and the effects of inebilizumab on these biomarkers in N-MOmentum. Methods N-MOmentum randomised participants to receive inebilizumab or placebo with a randomised controlled period (RCP) of 28 weeks and an open-label follow-up period of ≥2 years. The sNfL, sUCHL1, sTau and sGFAP were measured using single-molecule arrays in 1260 scheduled and attack-related samples from N-MOmentum participants (immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibodies to aquaporin-4-positive, myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein-IgG-positive or double autoantibody-negative) and two control groups (healthy donors and patients with relapsing–remitting multiple sclerosis). Results The concentration of all four biomarkers increased during NMOSD attacks. At attack, sNfL had the strongest correlation with disability worsening during attacks (Spearman R 2 =0.40; p=0.01) and prediction of disability worsening after attacks (sNfL cut-off 32 pg/mL; area under the curve 0.71 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.89); p=0.02), but only sGFAP predicted upcoming attacks. At RCP end, fewer inebilizumab-treated than placebo-treated participants had sNfL>16 pg/mL (22% vs 45%; OR 0.36 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.76); p=0.004). Conclusions Compared with sGFAP, sTau and sUCHL1, sNfL at attack was the strongest predictor of disability worsening at attack and follow-up, suggesting a role for identifying participants with NMOSD at risk of limited post-relapse recovery. Treatment with inebilizumab was associated with lower levels of sGFAP and sNfL than placebo. Trial registration number NCT02200770 . CLINICAL NEUROLOGY RANDOMISED TRIALS http://dx.doi.org/10.13039/100019637 Horizon Therapeutics N/A (funded study [formerly by Viela Bio/MedImmune special-feature unlocked WHAT IS ALREADY KNOWN ON THIS TOPIC Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is characterised by incremental permanent disability; thus, availability of biomarkers as indicators of the presence and progression of NMOSD is highly desirable. The aim of this study was to investigate the potential relationship between four putative biomarkers and disease activity/disability in participants from the N-MOmentum study and to assess the impact of inebilizumab treatment on their observed concentrations. WHAT THIS STUDY ADDS Serum neurofilament light chain measured at attack was the best predictor among biomarkers studied for disability worsening during and after attacks but was inferior to serum glial fibrillary acidic protein in prediction of future attacks. Compared with placebo, treatment with inebilizumab attenuated the elevation of biomarkers during attacks and reduced levels of these biomarkers over time in the absence of adjudicated attacks. HOW THIS STUDY MIGHT AFFECT RESEARCH, PRACTICE OR POLICY These findings may help to inform progress towards assessment of clinical status, prognosis and treatment decisions for patients with NMOSD by means of routine measurement of biomarkers. Introduction Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) is a rare autoimmune inflammatory disease of the central nervous system (CNS) characterised by attacks of optic neuritis, transverse myelitis and, less commonly, brain or brainstem inflammation. 1 Attacks are thought to be caused by astroglial injury resulting in secondary demyelination and substantial tissue injury. 2 Incremental damage occurs in the context of acute attacks, which can be severe and cause permanent disability due to incomplete recovery; in contrast to multiple sclerosis (MS), progressive worsening of disability independent of attacks is rare. 3 Immunoglobulin G (IgG) autoantibodies to aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG) are pathogenic; up to 90% of patients with NMOSD are AQP4-IgG seropositive (AQP4+). 4 5 In the CNS, AQP4-IgG binds to the extracellular domain of AQP4 expressed in the astrocyte, resulting in astrocytic damage through complement-mediated and complement-independent mechanisms. 6 7 Damaged astrocytes compromise trophic support for surrounding oligodendrocytes and neurons, presumably leading to secondary inflammation, demyelination and axonal loss. 8 Experimental data also suggest that AQP4-IgG induces cytokine production, increasing blood–brain barrier permeability. 9 Identifying biomarkers as indicators of the presence and course of disease promises to improve diagnosis and management of neurological conditions such as NMOSD. 10 Soluble glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), an abundant cytoskeletal intermediate filament in astrocytes, is released into cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and serum following astroglial injury. 11 Serum GFAP (sGFAP) was previously found to correlate strongly with NMOSD attacks, 12–14 including attack prediction. 14 Neurofilaments are structural proteins, exclusively expressed in neurons, forming an essential part of the cytoskeletal scaffold. 15 Axonal damage leads to elevated CSF and serum concentrations of neurofilament light chain (NfL) in the CSF and serum. 16 NfL was validated as a highly sensitive biomarker of neuroaxonal damage, regardless of cause, 17 and serum NfL (sNfL) is a biomarker of neuronal injury in various neurodegenerative diseases, as well as in NMOSD. 12 13 15 18 19 Ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCHL1) is a highly abundant neuron-specific protein that forms part of the ubiquitin proteasome system of protein degradation. 20 Tau forms an important part of the microtubule structure in the axonal cytoskeletion. 21 Neuronal damage causes release of UCHL1 and tau into CSF and plasma, and elevated serum levels have been observed in several neurological and neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer’s disease, epilepsy and MS. 15 22 GFAP, NfL, tau and UCHL1 concentration detection was previously limited to CSF; however, development of highly sensitive, single-molecule array (SIMOA) technology (Quanterix; Lexington, Massachusetts, USA) has allowed for reliable serum measurement. N-MOmentum was a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 2/3 trial assessing the efficacy and safety of inebilizumab, an anti-CD19, B-cell-depleting antibody, in participants with NMOSD. 1 23 The aim of the current study was to investigate potential relationships between sGFAP, sNfL, serum tau (sTau) and serum UCHL1 (sUCHL1), and disease activity in N-MOmentum study participants and to assess the impact of inebilizumab on concentrations of these putative biomarkers.

extracted_data.document_summary: This study investigated the relationships between serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL), ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (sUCHL1), tau (sTau), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP) levels with disease activity and disability in neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD), and the effects of inebilizumab on these biomarkers. It found that all four biomarkers increase during NMOSD attacks, reflecting CNS damage. Specifically, sNfL was the strongest predictor of post-attack disability worsening, while sGFAP was superior in predicting future attacks. Treatment with inebilizumab attenuated biomarker elevations during attacks and reduced sNfL and sGFAP levels over time.

treatment_details.dose_specificity: Participants were randomized to receive intravenous inebilizumab 300 mg or placebo (saline) on days 1 and 15 of a 28-week randomized controlled period (RCP), followed by an open-label follow-up period of at least 2 years. No specific dose-response comparisons for biomarker changes were reported, but inebilizumab treatment was associated with attenuated biomarker elevation during attacks and reduced biomarker levels over time compared to placebo.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly during NMOSD attacks (week before, on day of, and week following attacks), with mean concentrations exceeding an elevated level (>16 pg/mL) and remaining elevated >7 days post-attack. Showed the strongest correlation with disability worsening during attacks (Spearman R^2=0.40; p=0.01) and predicted disability worsening after attacks (sNfL cut-off 32 pg/mL; AUC 0.71 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.89); p=0.02). At RCP end, fewer inebilizumab-treated participants had sNfL>16 pg/mL compared to placebo (22% vs 45%; OR 0.36 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.76); p=0.004). Significantly lower in inebilizumab-treated compared to placebo-treated AQP4+ participants, and in attack-free participants. During attacks, levels were lower in inebilizumab-treated patients after RCP end (week 26 OLP, p=0.03 for median fold change from baseline). Elevated at baseline in 37% of AQP4+ NMOSD patients. Median sNfL was higher in placebo-treated participants with 3-month confirmed disability progression (55.3 pg/mL) versus those with no worsening (13.50 pg/mL).

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Structural protein exclusively expressed in neurons, forming part of the cytoskeletal scaffold; a highly sensitive biomarker of neuroaxonal damage and loss, reflecting CNS tissue injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: NMOSD attacks (acute and preceding), post-attack disability worsening, inebilizumab treatment, baseline in NMOSD (AQP4+, MOG+, double-negative) and RRMS patients, correlation with disability measures (EDSS, OSIS, mRS), relapse and remission phases of NMOSD, rituximab treatment, and subclinical disease activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Strongest predictor of disability worsening during and after attacks, useful for identifying NMOSD participants at risk of limited post-relapse recovery. Significantly correlates with EDSS ambulation subscale, pyramidal functional system, and mRS scores, and overall EDSS scores (Spearman R=0.40). Predicts EDSS score worsening at follow-up (AUC: 0.71). More sensitive for myelitis events. Lower levels with inebilizumab treatment indicate reduced CNS damage and attenuated attack-related elevation.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly during NMOSD attacks (week before, on day of, and week following attacks). Mean concentrations generally remained below the defined elevated level (>52 pg/mL). Proportions of participants with elevated baseline were similar across N-MOmentum populations. Levels were numerically lower after inebilizumab treatment in attack-free participants.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: Highly abundant neuron-specific protein involved in the ubiquitin proteasome system of protein degradation; serves as an indicator of Central Nervous System (CNS) damage and neuronal/axonal damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: NMOSD attacks (acute and preceding), evaluation of CNS damage in NMOSD patients, baseline in NMOSD patients, and in response to inebilizumab treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neuronal damage in neurological diseases and is associated with NMOSD attack severity and long-term disability. Not a significant predictor of upcoming attacks compared to sGFAP, nor as sensitive in predicting attacks or attack severity. Elevations did not occur independently of increased sGFAP and were not significantly associated with EDSS score changes after controlling for sNfL.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly during NMOSD attacks (week before, on day of, and week following attacks), showing statistically significant associations with attacks. Mean concentrations generally remained below the defined elevated level (>1.3 pg/mL). Proportions of participants with elevated baseline were similar across N-MOmentum populations. Levels were numerically lower after inebilizumab treatment in attack-free participants.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An important component of the microtubule structure in the axonal cytoskeleton; indicates neuronal and axonal damage, reflecting CNS tissue injury.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: NMOSD attacks, evaluation of CNS damage in NMOSD patients, baseline in NMOSD patients, and in response to inebilizumab treatment.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Indicates neuronal damage in neurological diseases and is associated with NMOSD attack severity, prediction of upcoming attacks, and long-term disability. Not a significant predictor of upcoming attacks compared to sGFAP, nor as sensitive in predicting attacks or attack severity. Elevations did not occur independently of increased sGFAP and were not significantly associated with EDSS score changes after controlling for sNfL.

measured_effect.magnitude_quantification: Increased significantly during NMOSD attacks and during the days before an attack, with mean concentrations increasing above an elevated level (>170 pg/mL). Levels returned to baseline after >7 days post-attack. Predicted upcoming attacks. Elevated at baseline versus healthy donors and RRMS patients (30% of AQP4+ participants had >170 pg/mL). Elevated baseline sGFAP in AQP4+ participants correlated with a Hazard Ratio of 2.56 for an adjudicated NMOSD attack. Treatment with inebilizumab was associated with lower levels than placebo, showing significantly lower levels in the absence of attack and smaller elevations during attacks.

analyzed_biomarkers.core_biological_function: An abundant cytoskeletal intermediate filament in astrocytes, released into CSF and serum following astroglial injury; a primary astrocytopathy marker, reflecting glial damage, CNS tissue injury, and inflammatory damage.
analyzed_biomarkers.relevant_activity_context: NMOSD attacks (acute and preceding), inebilizumab treatment, prediction of upcoming attacks, baseline in NMOSD (AQP4+, MOG+, double-negative) and RRMS patients, post-attack recovery, evaluation of CNS damage in NMOSD patients, and subclinical disease activity.
analyzed_biomarkers.performance_or_health_indicator: Superior predictor of upcoming NMOSD attacks and attack severity compared to sNfL, sTau, and sUCHL1. Associated with NMOSD attack severity, inflammatory damage, and disability worsening, including EDSS scores. May indicate subclinical disease activity. Lower levels with inebilizumab treatment indicate reduced astrocytic damage and attenuated attack-related elevation.
